tutorials.title: A forest floor for isopods
tutorials.summary: Make a ventilated leaf-litter habitat with a moist retreat and a drier side.
tutorials.materials:
Escape-proof ventilated container
Species-appropriate substrate
Pesticide-free hardwood leaf litter
Cork bark hide
Sphagnum moss
Suitable calcium source

steps.title: Start with the species
steps.body: Identify your isopods before building. Terrestrial species differ in ventilation and moisture needs; use a species-specific guide alongside these general steps.

steps.title: Choose a secure container
steps.body: Use an escape-resistant lid with ventilation. Keep furnishings and leaf litter below the rim so they do not create an escape route. Do not use a sealed jar.

steps.title: Add the substrate
steps.body: Add an appropriate substrate deep enough for your species to burrow. Avoid water pooling at the bottom.

steps.title: Make a moisture gradient
steps.body: Keep moss at one end damp, while allowing the opposite side to remain drier. The animals need a choice of conditions.

steps.title: Build the forest floor
steps.body: Add hardwood leaf litter and cork bark. Leaf litter serves as food and shelter; replenish it as it breaks down. Supply a suitable calcium source.

steps.title: Check and maintain
steps.body: Check moisture regularly, remove spoiled supplemental food, and maintain airflow. Adjust the wet end without soaking the whole enclosure.

tutorials.note: Never release captive isopods or used habitat materials outdoors. This is a habitat build, not a complete feeding or breeding guide.

sources.label: NEHERP — Isopod care and species differences

tutorials.title: A climbing habitat for crested geckos
tutorials.summary: Build upward with secure branches, leafy cover, and a carefully controlled environment.
tutorials.materials:
Tall, secure, well-ventilated vivarium
Sturdy branches and cork bark
Suitable live or artificial foliage
Species-appropriate substrate
Digital thermometers and hygrometer
Suitable UVB and lighting equipment
Thermostat for any heat source
Water dish and feeding ledge

steps.title: Plan upward
steps.body: Choose a tall vivarium for climbing. The RSPCA lists 45 × 45 × 60 cm (width × depth × height) as a minimum for one adult; provide more usable space where possible.

steps.title: Choose a stable location
steps.body: Keep the enclosure out of direct sun and away from draughts or radiators. Check the door and ventilation openings for escape gaps.

steps.title: Install environmental equipment
steps.body: Set up species-appropriate lighting, UVB, and any needed heat with a suitable thermostat. Use the linked care sheet for temperatures, UVB placement, and the day/night cycle.

steps.title: Secure the climbing routes
steps.body: Fix branches firmly at different heights. Add leafy cover and resting spaces without blocking airflow. Keep the feeding ledge and water accessible.

steps.title: Manage humidity
steps.body: Fit a hygrometer and follow the care sheet’s misting guidance. Provide ventilation and drying periods; constant wetness is not the goal.

steps.title: Run it before move-in
steps.body: Measure conditions at the animal’s resting and climbing positions across day and night. Check that temperatures and humidity remain appropriate before adding the gecko.

tutorials.note: Never house a gecko in a sealed decorative terrarium. This build guide does not replace complete species care, feeding, or veterinary advice.

tutorials.title: A dry habitat for leopard geckos
tutorials.summary: Create a roomy floor plan with warm and cool areas, secure hides, and a separate humid retreat.
tutorials.materials:
Secure, ventilated horizontal vivarium
Warm hide, cool hide, and humid hide
Suitable substrate or easy-clean initial flooring
Shallow water dish
Species-appropriate heat source and thermostat
Digital probe thermometers
Suitable UVB lighting and timer

steps.title: Give the floor room
steps.body: Choose a horizontal enclosure with space for movement and distinct warm and cool areas. The Royal Veterinary College recommends at least 36 × 18 × 18 inches; larger usable space is welcome.

steps.title: Set up the heat gradient
steps.body: Install a suitable heat source at one end, controlled by a compatible thermostat. Measure temperatures where the gecko actually rests. Follow the full care sheet for temperature targets.

steps.title: Place three retreats
steps.body: Provide hides on the warm and cool sides plus a separate humid hide for shedding. Keep general conditions dry; do not turn the whole habitat into a humid moss garden.

steps.title: Choose suitable flooring
steps.body: Select substrate for the animal’s age and health. Avoid calcium sand and rough or loose-loop carpet. An easy-clean initial setup helps you monitor a new animal.

steps.title: Arrange stable furnishings
steps.body: Secure heavy furnishings so digging cannot make them fall. Add a shallow water dish and safe cover while preserving walking routes.

steps.title: Verify before adding your gecko
steps.body: Install suitable UVB and a day/night cycle. Test the enclosure through several cycles and confirm the warm, cool, and humid areas against species care guidance.

tutorials.note: This is a dry vivarium build, not a closed tropical terrarium. Review the linked guidance for feeding, supplements, temperatures, and ongoing care.

sources.label: Royal Veterinary College — Leopard gecko care
